newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big reversal in Corporate Express.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big reversal in Corporate Express.

text.p: An investor seeing an arbitrage opportunity in the sharp selloff in shares of Corporate Express Inc did a sizable reverse conversion in the options, traders said Wednesday.
By about 1130 CST/1730 GMT, shares of the corporate supply vendor were down 8-5/16 at 10 on huge volume of more than 32 million shares.
The stock's daily volume averages about 822,000 shares.
The Corporate Express March 25 put and call each traded 13,000 contracts in what traders said was a reverse conversion by an institutional investor.
Harrison Roth, a senior options strategist at Cowen & Co, said the investor would have shorted the stock, sold the put and bought the call.
The 13,000 calls crossed in two blocks of 6,500 contracts, each at 1/16. They had no open interest.
The 13,000 puts also crossed in two blocks of 6,500 contracts. But they went off at 14-7/8. They did not have any open interest either.
"I think the customer did it to get short the stock," Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said of the options trades.
"There's no open interest in either one of them," he said. "If there's no open interest (in the puts) tomorrow, the customer exercised to get short the stock.
Typical reverse converions, also known as reversals, are done by combining a short underlying position with long call and short put positions.
A long call and short put position is a synthetic long underlying position.
Reversals are usually done to take advantage of arbitrage opportunities that arise when put/call parity is out of alignment.
Broadly, put/call parity is the price relationship between puts, calls, underlying securities and exercise prices.
